notes.claim: The modulus is the distance of the point (a, b) from the origin, and it is never negative.
The argument is the angle between the positive real axis and the line from the origin to the point.
A complex number with modulus r and argument theta is written r angle theta.
When finding the angle with an inverse tangent, check the quadrant, because a calculator’s answer may not be in the correct one.
Going back from length and angle: the across part is r cos theta and the up part is r sin theta.

sources.title: 7.4 The polar form — mathcentre
sources.quote: The distance of the point (a, b) from the origin is called the modulus, or magnitude of the complex number and has the symbol r. Alternatively, r is written as |z|. The modulus is never negative.

sources.title: 7.4 The polar form — mathcentre
sources.quote: The angle between the positive x axis and a line joining (a, b) to the origin is called the argument of the complex number.

sources.title: 7.4 The polar form — mathcentre
sources.quote: When the modulus and argument of a complex number, z, are known we write the complex number as z = r∠θ.

sources.title: 7.4 The polar form — mathcentre
sources.quote: but care must be taken when using a calculator to find an inverse tangent that the solution obtained is in the correct quadrant.

sources.quote: x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ
